words.meaning: To satisfy your thirst, or to put out a fire.
words.example: She drank a glass of cold water to quench her thirst after the race.

words.meaning: Spreading quickly and widely, often in an uncontrolled way.
words.example: Rumors spread rampant through the school before the exam results were posted.

words.meaning: To examine something very closely and carefully.
words.example: The teacher scrutinized every line of the essay for spelling mistakes.

words.meaning: Able to be touched or clearly seen; real and definite.
words.example: Winning the trophy was tangible proof of the team's hard work.

words.meaning: To undo or untangle something, or to solve a mystery.
words.example: The detective worked patiently to unravel the strange case.

words.meaning: To prove that someone was right or innocent after doubt.
words.example: The test results vindicated her original answer.

words.meaning: Good for your health, or morally good and decent.
words.example: The school canteen now serves more wholesome meals.

words.meaning: To produce a result, or to give way under pressure.
words.example: Careful studying will yield better exam results.

words.meaning: The highest point or peak of something.
words.example: The singer reached the zenith of her career after the world tour.

words.meaning: Sudden and unexpected.
words.example: The bus came to an abrupt stop when the light turned red.

words.meaning: Quick and energetic.
words.example: They took a brisk walk around the field before class started.

words.meaning: To gently persuade someone to do something.
words.example: She coaxed her little brother into finishing his homework.

words.meaning: Seeming difficult or frightening to deal with.
words.example: The final exam felt daunting, but she prepared well.

words.meaning: Serving as an excellent example; outstanding.
words.example: His exemplary behavior earned him the class monitor badge.

words.meaning: A natural talent or stylish quality.
words.example: She has a flair for painting colorful murals.

words.meaning: To measure or judge something carefully.
words.example: The coach asked questions to gauge how ready the team felt.

words.meaning: Understanding an event clearly only after it has happened.
words.example: In hindsight, he should have started studying earlier.

words.meaning: To light something up, or to make an idea clear.
words.example: The lamp helped illuminate the dark study room.

words.meaning: A special skill or ability to do something easily.
words.example: She has a knack for solving puzzles quickly.

words.meaning: Very generous or luxurious.
words.example: The school held a lavish celebration for its 50th anniversary.
